svg.text: Figure 3-2 · System FMEA failure chains — sheet 5 of 8
SFM rev 0.35 · BL-007 · draft · SFM-018 … SFM-025 · 15 causes on this sheet
FAILURE CAUSE · O · D · AP · ACTIONS (STEPS 4–6)
F4 Driver override: release control on brake
or cancel; yield lateral to steering input and
End effect: Delayed evasive maneuver or loss of control
Driver torque threshold too high or signal parsed wrong
Controller keeps commanding torque during override
The panda envelope passes STEERING_LKA torque that opposes
the driver while the driver overrides: the Toyota LKA check covers
magnitude, rate and measured-torque error only, and…
End effect: Driver must use brake to disengage
Button message parsed wrong or missing
End effect: Driver cannot accelerate out of a situation (e.g.
Stock cruise stays engaged after LionDriver disengages
End effect: Driver believes automation is off (mode confusion)
Cancel message not packed/sent for this car
F5 Driver monitoring: detect inattention and
escalate alerts; lock out engagement after
End effect: Driver not available to handle F1/F2 failures or
DM model false negative (eyes off road classified attentive)
Pose thresholds/calibration wrong for driver or mount
Driver camera or IR illumination degraded
Driver monitoring runs in demo mode while the item is engaged
(IsDriverViewEnabled left set): the policy uses a synthetic vehicle
state and the monitored seat can switch, so the actual driver may…
End effect: Driver not ready when takeover needed
Policy timers or recovery factor misconfigured
Low-speed or always-on exemption applied incorrectly
End effect: Driver annoyance; may reduce trust or prompt
Terminal driver-unresponsive state does not bring the item
End effect: No fallback if the driver is incapacitated
Defect in the minimum-risk manoeuvre of TSR-633 (#372): the latch
in minimum_risk.py not set or cleared while the item is still
engaged, controlsd not keeping forceDecel on while…

S = severity of the failure mode (max of its effects); O / D = occurrence / detection of the cause; “in <element>” = structure element where the cause lies; “→” = linked failure mode in another FMEA; hazard = HARA hazard of an end effect.
